name: json-voorhees
listed_description: JSON library for C++. Support for C++11. No dependencies, fast and dev-friendly.
reason: README says only 'a reasonably fast parser' with no numbers and the repo has no benchmark or perf directory (top level lists .github, config, doc, include, packaging, scripts, src; doc holds only conversions.dot, conversions.png, meme.jpg). Loki-Astari/json_performance (Aug 2024, M1, Clang 15) does not include it. A web search snippet (page not opened) attributes a third-party shootout row to it that is slower than both nlohmann/json and RapidJSON, so no evidence of beating any baseline.

name: JsonCpp
listed_description: A C++ library for interacting with JSON.
reason: README states 'We are not competing with SIMD-accelerated or reflection-based parsers' and makes no speed claim. In the nativejson-benchmark sample CSV (JsonCpp 1.0.0 vs nlohmann v2.0.3, Core i7-4980HQ, clang 7.0) JsonCpp parses slower than nlohmann on all three files (canada 142.458 vs 55.591 ms, citm_catalog 14.587 vs 9.875, twitter 8.477 vs 7.010) and loses canada stringify (84.443 vs 76.315 ms); only citm_catalog stringify (5.679 vs 7.178 ms) and twitter stringify (4.139 vs 4.239 ms) are marginally ahead, which nobody claims.

name: jsonParse
listed_description: A simple JSON parser in ANSI C.
reason: README claims 'jsonParse is faster than cJSON and json-c' but gives no numbers, method or benchmark; the repo has parse.c, parse.h, object.c, object.h and a test folder with a demo (testStr.c) only, and 9 commits. A web search found no third-party benchmark. Directional claim without numbers.

name: jute
reason: README makes no speed claim and the repo (jute.h, jute.cpp, main.cpp, test_jute.cpp, Makefile, data.json) has no benchmark; it states it does no error checking and assumes valid JSON. A web search found no third-party benchmark that includes it.
